notes.2: This question was challenging for many candidates. Most candidates clearly saw the term “distance travelled” and immediately looked at the area under the graph in each section, without noticing that the complete phrase was “distance travelled per second”, which they should have been able to interpret as speed.
notes.4: Most candidates recognised that weight is measured in newtons.
notes.5: Candidates showed a good understanding of the concept that mass is independent of the gravitational field, but weight is dependent on it.
notes.9: This question was answered well and candidates thought their way through the problem clearly and recognised that the centre of mass of the lamina moved towards the bottom of the page.
notes.14: The majority of candidates incorrectly thought that the width of the tube would alter the height of the liquid column and showed little understanding of this method of measuring pressure.
notes.17: Many candidates thought that the container with the larger thermal capacity would have the higher temperature. They failed to recognise that the larger the thermal capacity of the container, the more energy is transferred from the water to the container.
notes.18: This question was usually answered correctly.
notes.19: This question was challenging for many candidates. Some thought that the density of a fluid did not decrease with rising temperature and others thought that convection does not help an even temperature distribution in a pan of water when it is heated. Few recognised that the phrase, “heat rises”, is an incorrect common belief.
notes.21: Stronger candidates answered correctly. However, many candidates correctly identified the change of direction of propagation of the waves, but incorrectly thought that the wavelength (and hence the speed) of the waves would decrease on entering the deep water.
notes.23: The question was answered well and candidates showed an understanding that the rays from a point on an object converge and intersect at a point after refraction at the lens.
notes.29: The question was not answered well by many candidates. Candidates needed to take care when reading instruments where the scale divisions are not equivalent to 1 or 0.1, etc.
notes.30: The majority of candidates understood how ammeters and voltmeters are connected into a circuit.
notes.31: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly.
notes.32: In this question candidates either did not recognise the circuit diagram symbol of the thermistor or did not recognise that the thermistor is a temperature dependent device.
notes.33: The most common error in this question was for candidates to fail to recognise that the transformer is an a.c. device and will not produce an output using d.c.
notes.34: Many candidates did not recognise that the role of either a circuit-breaker or a fuse is to disconnect the live wire from the appliance and so did not select the correct answer.
notes.35: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly.
